history.content: My AWS bill jumped from $90 to $400 this month. Figure out why.

Found it, per AWS's own billing email from this month: Your estimated bill is $402.11, and the top line item is Amazon EC2 at about $310, driven by data transfer out of us east 1. That's the jump, roughly $300 of data egress you weren't paying before. Common culprits for a sudden egress spike: a new public facing workload (downloads, video, backups syncing off cloud), a misconfigured bucket or instance serving large files publicly, or something hammering your endpoints from outside. Two things I can do next: 1. Check your Drive or mail for any recent deploys or project changes that might explain new traffic. 2. Draft a note to AWS support (or whoever manages the account) asking for a per service, per resource breakdown of the us east 1 transfer charges. Want either?
